subject: Medford High School Building Project
overview: The Medford High School Building Committee hosted its seventh community forum to update the public on the high school building project. School leaders and the design team presented updates on the educational plan, architectural design, construction phasing, total cost estimates, and the timeline leading to a June 2026 debt exclusion vote.

items.title: Welcome and Agenda Overview
items.summary: Building Committee Chair Jenny Graham welcomed attendees and introduced the forum's agenda covering educational priorities, building design, construction phasing, project costs, and next steps.

items.title: Educational Plan and Project Goals
items.summary: Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi detailed how the educational plan guides the project by expanding Career and Technical Education (CTE) from 17 to 19 shops, integrating the Curtis Tufts program, improving accessibility, and maintaining community services such as Kids' Corner and the Medford Family Network.

items.title: Architectural Design and Site Layout
items.summary: Design team architects and civil engineers presented the preferred addition-renovation design, which preserves and renovates the existing pool and gymnasium while surrounding them with integrated academic and vocational spaces, net-zero sustainability features, and reconfigured athletic fields.

items.title: Construction Phasing Strategy
items.summary: Matt Rice outlined a three-phase construction sequence designed to keep the existing school operational on-site without the use of temporary modular classrooms.

items.title: Project Costs, Reimbursement, and Timeline
items.summary: Jenny Graham explained that design efficiencies reduced the total project cost estimate from $850 million to under $700 million, with an estimated $215 million in MSBA reimbursement anticipated prior to the June 8 debt exclusion vote.

items.title: Community Outreach and Schedule
items.summary: The committee presented upcoming public engagement opportunities, including school building committee meetings, future community forums, and joint meetings with the City Council.

items.title: Public Question and Answer Session
items.summary: Panelists answered public questions regarding student enrollment capacity, baseline code upgrade costs versus new construction, traffic and transit mitigation, fundraising efforts, and CTE student involvement during construction.
